 ORDER

This appeal by the claimant under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 09.11.2019 passed by MACT, Neemuch in MACC No.04/2018 seeking enhancement of the amount of compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
2. The date of accident, negligence and the issue of liability are not in dispute and the findings recorded by the Tribunal in this regard are also not in question.

As per the findings of the Tribunal,
for the permanent disability suffered by the appellant/claimant, the Tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,71,972/- along with interest.

The break up of the compensation amount is as under:

Permanent disability -Rs.7,25,760/- (i.e. Rs.4500 1800(40% future prospects)=6300x12=75600 x 60% (permanent disability)=45360x16 (multiplier))
Medical expenses -Rs.2,40,712/-
 Attender -Rs.10,500/-
 Transportation -Rs.10,000/-
 Special diet -Rs.10,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.75,000/-
 ----------------
 TOTAL Rs.10,71,972/-
 ===========
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the Tribunal has committed an error in awarding just and proper amount of compensation in the case as the amount awarded by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the injured.
The injured has suffered 60% permanent disability and his leg was amputated from below the knee.
He remained in hospital for treatment long period.

He was out of job for three months on account of the accident, however, no amount of compensation has been awarded by the Tribunal on that account, therefore, prays for just and proper amount of compensation in the case.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has argued in support of the impugned award and contended that the Claims Tribunal has rightly awarded the compensation amount in the case which does not call for any interference by this Court.
5. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and going through the record, I find substance in the arguments advanced by the counsel for the appellant.
In the considered opinion of this Court, the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the income of the injured at Rs.4500/- per month which deserves to be enhanced to Rs.6,000/- per month.
The Tribunal has also not awarded any compensation under the head of loss of income during the period of treatment.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, in the considered opinion of this Court, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal deserves to be enhanced as under:
Permanent disability -Rs.9,67,680/- (i.e. Rs.6000 2400 (40% future prospects)=8400x12=1,00,800x60%(PD)=60480x15=9,07,200/-
 Loss of wages -Rs.18,000/- (i.e. Rs.6000x3)

Medical expenses -Rs.2,40,700/-
 Attender -Rs.20,000/-
 Transportation -Rs.25,000/-

Special diet -Rs.25,000/-
 Pain & suffering -Rs.1,00,000/-
Devilal @ Devinath vs Dhanraj Sharma on 14 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10824503/
2  -------------------
 TOTAL Rs.13,35,900/-
 =============
6.
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the case is Rs.13,35,900/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.10,71,972/-.

Accordingly, the appellant is entitled to an additional sum of Rs.2,63,928/--
over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
7. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation amount by a sum of Rs.2,63,928
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE hk/
